title: Correlation-Guided Flow Matching with Annealed Masking for Spatial Transcriptomics Generation
abstract: arXiv:2609.22187v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) provides spatially resolved gene expression profiling but remains expensive, motivating the prediction of ST from histology images. Generative models have emerged as a mainstream paradigm for ST prediction due to their ability to model the conditional distribution of gene expression and capture its inherent stochasticity. However, these methods typically treat genes as independent prediction targets and overlook the intrinsic gene-gene interactions in biological systems, which limits their ability to preserve biologically meaningful co-expression patterns. We argue that gene-gene interactions, which reflect shared pathways and regulatory mechanisms, are essential for generating numerically accurate and biologically coherent ST profiles. translated_title: 用于空间转录组学生成的相关性引导流匹配与退火掩码方法
translated_abstract: 空间转录组学（ST）能够提供空间分辨的基因表达谱分析，但其成本高昂，这促使研究者尝试从组织学图像预测空间转录组数据。生成模型因其能够对基因表达的条件分布进行建模并捕捉其固有的随机性，已成为ST预测的主流范式。然而，这些方法通常将基因视为独立的预测目标，忽视了生物系统中基因间固有的相互作用，这限制了它们保留具有生物学意义的共表达模式的能力。我们认为，反映共享通路和调控机制的基因间相互作用，对于生成数值准确且生物学上连贯的ST谱至关重要。在本文中，我们提出了CorrFlow，一个用于组织学图像到ST预测的相关性引导流匹配框架，它通过两个互补的……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 提出CorrFlow框架，利用相关性引导的流匹配和退火掩码显式建模基因间依赖关系，从而从组织学图像生成数值更准确、生物学上更连贯的空间转录组谱。
en_tdlr: Proposes CorrFlow, a correlation-guided flow matching framework with annealed masking that explicitly models gene-gene dependencies to generate numerically accurate and biologically coherent spatial transcriptomics profiles from histology images.
